physical_skill: Hold a loose 10 g float valve in its 6 mm hole by pressing its 10 mm flat top on the lid's top face with one gripper, while the other picks a 2 g, 12 mm silicone cap off the counter, turns its open end to face the lid, lines it up with the 5 mm valve end on the underside and pushes it about 1 N over the sprung end knob until its lip snaps into the groove, then both let go and withdraw.
valid_shortcuts: GPU red team on this task.py (media/demo-redteam_*): do nothing 0; one arm only (cap pushed without holding the valve) 0, valve pushed out past 10 mm, latched; cap held on rather than released 0; cap pushed only part way 0 in the simulation (it drops off when released; 0.25 only if it stays on the end, still and hands clear). Scripted demo 1.0 in two fresh runs on the final source (06:44 and 06:49 local). Dream-1 0.0. A cap on the counter or elsewhere is 0; the valve fallen-out record is latched until reset.
distinct_from_nearest: No accepted, pending or revising task refits a pressure cooker's float valve or its silicone cap, or any push-on cap onto a loose part held in from the opposite face. Nearest is 2291 (stovetop lid closing), the same appliance family with a different operation.
